requirements.title: Input/output rounding mode can be specified by OPEN, data transfer, or edit descriptor
requirements.definition: The input/output rounding mode can be specified by an OPEN statement, a data transfer statement, or an edit descriptor.

pending.round-mode-open-specifier: Unassertable as an internal-file byte oracle in this packet: OPEN ROUND= requires external-file connection semantics from clause 12. Future external-file fixtures must name the file connection, descriptor, value, and exact record bytes.
pending.round-mode-data-transfer-specifier: After clause 12 data-transfer ROUND= ownership, internal WRITE(buf,'(F4.1)',ROUND='UP') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.3'; 1.25 is exactly representable and UP chooses the smallest representable decimal output not less than the internal value.
pending.round-mode-edit-descriptor: After 13.8.8 RU ownership, internal WRITE(buf,'(RU,F4.1)') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.3'.

requirements.title: Decimal value and internal value distinguish exact decimal text from stored approximation
requirements.definition: A decimal value is the exact decimal number represented by a character string, while an internal value is the number actually stored; formatted output converts internal to decimal value and input converts decimal to internal value.

pending.decimal-value-defined: Documentation/source-use plan: fixture rationales must compute exact decimal strings separately from binary internal approximations.
pending.internal-value-defined: Documentation/source-use plan: fixture rationales must not treat 0.1 as exactly stored unless the processor representation supports it.
pending.formatted-output-conversion-direction: Future rounding fixtures must derive expected output from the internal value, not from source-token spelling.
pending.formatted-input-conversion-direction: Future input fixtures must derive expected stored approximation from the decimal value and rounding mode.

requirements.title: Rounding modes define required conversion directions and processor-dependent tie/default cases
requirements.definition: UP, DOWN, ZERO, NEAREST, COMPATIBLE, and PROCESSOR_DEFINED prescribe conversion rounding as stated; NEAREST ties and PROCESSOR_DEFINED default are processor dependent as specified.

pending.round-up-conversion: After 13.8.8, internal WRITE(buf,'(RU,F4.1)') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.3'.
pending.round-down-conversion: After 13.8.8, internal WRITE(buf,'(RD,F4.1)') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.2'.
pending.round-zero-conversion: After 13.8.8, internal WRITE(buf,'(RZ,F4.1)') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.2'.
pending.round-nearest-conversion: After 13.8.8, internal WRITE(buf,'(RN,F4.1)') 1.0 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.0'; this exact case avoids the processor-dependent halfway rule.
pending.round-nearest-tie-processor-dependent: Unassertable as a unique string under p3 alone: internal WRITE(buf,'(RN,F4.1)') 1.25 is halfway between ' 1.2' and ' 1.3', and p3 makes the NEAREST tie choice processor dependent.
pending.round-compatible-conversion: After 13.8.8, internal WRITE(buf,'(RC,F4.1)') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.3' because COMPATIBLE chooses the value away from zero at halfway.
pending.round-processor-defined-latitude: Unassertable as a unique string: PROCESSOR_DEFINED selects a processor-dependent default mode, so internal WRITE(buf,'(RP,F4.1)') 1.25 may not have one portable expected field.

requirements.title: NEAREST corresponds to ISO IEEE round-to-nearest on processors supporting IEEE conversion rounding
requirements.definition: On processors that support IEEE rounding on conversions, NEAREST corresponds to ISO/IEC 60559:2020 round to nearest.

pending.nearest-ieee-round-to-nearest: Guarded by IEEE conversion-rounding support under clause 17, internal WRITE(buf,'(RN,F4.1)') 1.25 to character(len=4) expects exactly buf=' 1.2' because ISO round-to-nearest chooses the even last digit for this halfway decimal conversion.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, three rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_137.json. The reviewer re-derived unit hashes and read Tables 13.1, 13.2 and 13.3 ROW BY ROW against the PDF, independently of the author's reconstruction - necessary because extraction interleaved the columns and every future E/EN/ES fixture derives from those rows. THREE blocking findings. The integrator found the first directly: two sample plans gave a NEGATIVE result for the POSITIVE input 0.5, but SS suppresses the optional plus so the sign position must be BLANK - corrected to ' 500.000E-03' and '   5.000E-01', hand-derived and corroborated with gfortran. C137SR-001: ELEVEN units mixing an obligation with a grant of latitude were dispositioned wholly as permission - the fourth occurrence of that class this session - and were re-dispositioned to requirements with the latitude confined to rationale and oracle text; the reviewer confirmed no latitude is now wrongly asserted as an obligation. C137SR-002: placeholder plans remained, saying things like 'future plan must include exact output'; 48 entries were changed, 21 upgraded to exact executable strings and 27 marked explicitly unassertable, and the reviewer independently derived the scale-factor cases -1P,E10.3E2 giving ' 0.010E+02' and 1P,E10.3E2 giving ' 1.000E+00'. R1323 carries no diagnostic facet because it defines a hex-digit-string form and prohibits nothing. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977.
